title: From Skill Extraction to Multistakeholder Recommendation: A Two-Stage Framework for Bias Governance in Skills-Based Job Matching

bias_targets.methodology: Distributional auditing of historical skill assignments to identify male- or female-dominated clusters, and counterfactual testing by systematically replacing gender-coded linguistic expressions (e.g., pronouns, stereotyped terms) in interview transcripts to observe changes in skill extraction.

Distributional auditing to identify over- and underrepresentation of EU-protected groups (e.g., ethnic origin, religion, disability, age) in historical data, counterfactual testing by injecting stereotypical phrases into neutral transcripts, and evaluating candidate-side demographic parity of recommended jobs against historical baselines.
Tracking measures such as popularity lift to evaluate individual-level fairness and exposure in candidate-job recommendations.
